title: 2003 AMC 12A Problem 17
statement: Square \(ABCD\) has sides of length \(4,\) and \(M\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{CD}.\) A circle with radius \(2\) and center \(M\) intersects a circle with radius \(4\) and center \(A\) at points \(P\) and \(D.\) What is the distance from \(P\) to \(\overline{AD}?\)

solutions.text:
Place \(D=(0,0),\) \(C=(4,0),\) and \(A=(0,4).\) The circle centered at \(M=(2,0)\) is \((x-2)^2+y^2=4,\) and the circle centered at \(A\) is \(x^2+(y-4)^2=16.\)

Solving these equations gives the intersection \(P=\left(\dfrac{16}{5},\dfrac85\right).\)

Since \(\overline{AD}\) lies on the \(y\)-axis, the distance from \(P\) to \(\overline{AD}\) is its \(x\)-coordinate, \(\dfrac{16}{5}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Put \(D\) at the origin with \(A\) on the \(y\)-axis and \(C\) on the \(x\)-axis
The distance from \(P\) to \(\overline{AD}\) is the \(x\)-coordinate of \(P\)
